items.title: Peel Police Data Shows Nearly Seven Vehicles Stolen a Day Across Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Regional Police's online crime mapping portal recorded 229 vehicle thefts across Mississauga, Brampton and Toronto over the past month. According to the data, the thefts occurred between Sept. 12 and Oct. 12, averaging roughly seven incidents a day region-wide. The outlet found Mississauga logged the most cases at 133, while Brampton followed with 94 and Toronto accounted for two more. Automobiles made up the large majority of stolen vehicles, totaling 157, or about 69 per cent, followed by 48 trucks and 19 motorcycles, with five other vehicles rounding out the count. Insauga.com says several thefts clustered near Toronto Pearson International Airport, including two cars taken from Viscount Road on Sept. 17 and Sept. 25. Additional incidents were reported nearby on Terminal Three Road during the same stretch.

items.title: Thanksgiving Monday: What’s Open and Closed in Toronto and Southern Ontario
items.summary: Thanksgiving Monday is here, and many stores, businesses, government offices and services will be closed or operating on reduced hours across Toronto and southern Ontario today. Thanksgiving falls on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, with closures and holiday hours expected in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Hamilton, Halton, Durham, Niagara and other cities and towns across Ontario. Thanksgiving has been officially celebrated as an annual holiday in Canada since Nov. 6, 1879 and is traditionally observed on the second Monday in October. In 1957, Governor General Vincent Massey issued a proclamation establishing the second Monday in October as a day of thanksgiving for Canada’s annual harvest. Thanksgiving is a statutory holiday in Ontario and most of Canada, although its status differs in Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick. Here’s a look at what’s open and closed on Thanksgiving Monday in: In Mississauga, a number of places will be open Oct. 12, including Square One Shopping Centre (including the Walmart Supercentre, Food District and Rec Room locations in the mall), Whole Foods Square One, T&T Supermarket, most cafes, restaurants and bars that are typically open on Mondays (call ahead to confirm), some smaller grocery stores (such as Rabba locations), most Shoppers Drug Mart locations, YMCA locations, movie theatres and most gas stations and convenience stores. All government offices at all levels of government, including City Hall, will be closed.

items.title: Late Goal and Shootout Heroics Lift Mississauga Rebels to Wendy Dufton Memorial Title
items.summary: CHL.ca reports the Mississauga Rebels rallied from a third-period deficit to win the 2026 Wendy Dufton Memorial U16 AAA championship, beating Detroit's Victory Honda 2-1 in a shootout at Western Fair Sports Centre in London. According to the recap, Mississauga trailed 1-0 late in regulation before tying the game with just 13 seconds left on the clock. Neither team scored in overtime, sending the final to a shootout, where Mateo Georgy and Liam Kozlowski both converted for the Rebels. Goaltender David Stewart stopped Luke Rowe's attempt, and Anthony Shipway missed the net for Victory Honda, sealing the win. The title capped a four-day run for Mississauga that included a 2-1 semifinal victory over the North York Rangers. The tournament, hosted by the London Junior Knights from Oct. 8 to 11, drew 40 U16 AAA teams from Ontario and the United States as an early look at prospects eligible for the 2027 OHL Priority Selection. Georgy led the champions with 11 points over eight games, while teammates Max Kopec and Gavin Laughlin each added nine.

items.title: Insults and Old Rivalries Resurface as Parrish and Crombie Face Off in Mississauga's Mayoral Race
items.summary: CTV News reports tensions have boiled over in Mississauga's mayoral race, now effectively a rematch between incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor, Bonnie Crombie. The outlet traces the rivalry back to 2024, when Crombie stepped down after a decade as mayor to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, clearing the way for longtime councillor Parrish to win the byelection that followed. According to CTV, Crombie resigned as Liberal leader after the party's February 2025 provincial election loss and announced over the summer that she would seek her old job back, setting up a clash with Parrish, who at 80 is campaigning for a second term. The report notes 14 candidates are on the ballot in total, with Ward 2's Alvin Tedjo and Ward 7's Dipika Damerla also drawing attention as frontrunners. CTV says the hostility spilled into public view at a recent debate, where Parrish dismissed Crombie as the blond bombshell and claimed city staff were terrified she might return, while Crombie shot back that staff actually feared Parrish and accused her of staying in her office instead of doing the job.

items.title: 2026 Mississauga election: Meet the candidates running for Peel District School Board trustee in Wards 3 and 4
items.summary: Voice the Vote will include 15 local organizers and provide … Susan Benjamin, Mohamed Elghamry, Avtar Ghotra and Marina Qu… Three candidates are vying to fill the seat left vacant by retiring trustee Sue Lawton. Three candidates are running to represent Mississauga wards 3 and 4 on the Peel District School Board. Three candidates are vying for the Mississauga Wards 3 and 4 seat on the Peel District School Board (PDSB). The electoral area’s sitting trustee, Sue Lawton, is not seeking re-election so there is no incumbent in the race. To help voters get to know the candidates, Metroland Media submitted a questionnaire to everyone on the ballot. Here is what they had to say. items.title: Retired Teacher Seeks Re-Election as Three Challengers Join Peel School Board’s Ward 5 Trustee Race
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports four candidates, Susan Benjamin, Mohamed Elghamry, Avtar Ghotra and Marina Qureshi, are competing for the Peel District School Board trustee seat in Mississauga Ward 5 in the 2026 municipal election. According to the outlet, Metroland sent a questionnaire to every name on the ballot and published the responses, edited for length and clarity, so voters could compare the field. Benjamin, who told Metroland she is the incumbent English Public trustee for Ward 5, described herself as a retired teacher with more than 40 years in the classroom. She said that includes 15 years with the Peel and Dufferin-Peel Catholic school boards, and that she has lived in Mississauga for 26 years. Benjamin added she is not affiliated with any political party and said she has worked well with elected officials at the municipal, provincial and federal levels across her two previous terms on the board. The Ward 5 trustee race is one of several school board contests on the ballot alongside Mississauga's mayoral and council races this election.

items.title: New Poll Finds Younger and Older Mississauga Voters Split Sharply Over Hazel McCallion's Legacy
items.summary: According to a new Liaison Strategies survey, Hazel McCallion's legacy carries far more weight with older Mississauga voters than with younger ones heading into the mayoral race. The poll found 75 per cent of residents 65 and older say her legacy matters when picking a mayor, compared with just 29 per cent of those aged 18 to 34. Liaison reports the finding stands out as incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie defend their records against councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, framing the race as a contest between experience and change. Overall, the survey found 49 per cent of residents call McCallion's legacy important, even as 52 per cent say a candidate claiming to have learned from her wouldn't change their vote. Liaison Strategies says it surveyed 1,000 Mississauga residents by phone between Oct. 2 and Oct. 4 using interactive voice recording technology, weighting the results to match 2021 Census targets. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin said the campaign has become an argument over who can best lead the city, whether that's the sitting mayor, a returning former mayor, or a councillor promising change.

items.title: Decades of City Hall Experience Collide in Mississauga's Four-Way Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to the Pointer, Mississauga's next mayor will take on outsized powers at a moment when affordability, housing and growing congestion are testing the city's limits for its more than 800,000 residents. The outlet reports crime has also risen to the top of the City Hall agenda heading into the vote. The Pointer profiles four front-running candidates: councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. The outlet notes Tedjo and Damerla both challenged Parrish in the 2024 mayoral by-election that first put her in office, while Crombie is seeking a return to the job she held for more than nine years before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberals. The Pointer reports Damerla brings nearly eight years on council and seven years as a provincial MPP for Mississauga, while Tedjo has served roughly four years at the council level. According to the outlet, all four candidates are centering their campaigns on affordability, crime and transportation, with Damerla also making City Hall accountability a signature issue.

items.title: Mississauga's Next Hospital Carries a $1-Billion Price Tag, and Fundraisers Are Two-Thirds There
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Trillium Health Partners Foundation has launched a $1-billion fundraising campaign called Built for Us to help build what's billed as Canada's largest hospital, the future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital. The outlet reports the new facility will replace the existing Mississauga Hospital and include the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, described as the province's first hospital dedicated specifically to women's and children's health. Foundation president and CEO Caroline Riseboro told Mississauga.com the campaign builds on funding already committed by the province and the City of Mississauga, plus transformational support from private donors. Riseboro said the foundation has raised about $600 million so far and is aiming to close the remaining $400 million gap by 2032. Mississauga.com reports the Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital is expected to open in late 2033 or early 2034.

items.title: A Mississauga Ticket-Holder Says She's Heard Nothing a Month After a Comedy Festival Fell Through
items.summary: According to CTV News Toronto, ticket-holder Brenna Oude-Reimerink says she still hasn't gotten a refund a month after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival was abruptly postponed. The outlet reports the festival was scheduled to run Sept. 11 to 13 at Erindale Park near the University of Toronto Mississauga, with headliners including Stavros Halkias, John Mulaney and Jeff Arcuri. CTV News Toronto says Oude-Reimerink paid roughly $394 for two VIP tickets through a third-party ticket seller, expecting exclusive entry lanes and table service. She told the outlet she and her sister had been especially excited to see Arcuri perform live for the first time. CTV News Toronto reports organizers sent a detailed logistics email on Sept. 7, then abruptly announced the postponement the very next day without giving a clear reason. The outlet says festival organizers offered only a brief public statement calling the postponement the right call to deliver the best possible festival.
